National Insurance Company Ltd, ... vs Shaik Khaleel, Adilabad
Dist 1 Other on 21 April, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice M.G. Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.650 of 2017
Judgment:

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd, ... vs Shaik Khaleel, Adilabad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This appeal is preferred by National Insurance Company Limited, questioning the award and decree, dated 29.11.2016 passed in O.P.No.416 of 2012 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Adilabad (for short, the Tribunal).
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Adilabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties have been referred to as arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.75,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident that occurred on 27.02.2012.

It is stated that on the fateful day, while the claimant was standing on the left side of Cinema Road in front of Ganesh Talkies, at about 14:00 hours, one car bearing No. AP 01 H 0564, owned by respondent No. 1, insured with respondent No. 2, being driven by its driver, came in a rash and negligent manner from Netaji Chowk with high speed and dashed the claimant from behind.
As a result, the claimant fracture of left leg and other bleeding injuries all over the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to Akhil Orthopedic Hospital, Adilabad and thereafter shifted to RIMS, Adilabad, for MGP, J Macma_650_2017 better treatment.

He spent Rs.25,000/-
towards medical and incidental charges.
Due to the said accident, he sustained permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.
Therefore, he laid the claim against the respondents seeking compensation of Rs.75,000/- under various heads.

4. Before the Tribunal, while the respondent No. 1 remained ex parte, the respondent No. 2 filed counter denying the averments made in the claim petition, the age, occupation, injuries, treatment and income of the claimant and further contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the crime vehicle i.e., Car bearing No. AP 01 H 0564 as the claimant himself was on the road without observing the vehicular traffic on the road and suddenly came into contact of the moving car resulting into accident.
Lastly contended that the compensation claimed by the claimant is highly excess and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Considering the claim and the counter filed by the respondent No. 2 and on evaluation of the evidence, both oral and documentary, the learned Tribunal has partly allowed the O.P. and awarded compensation of Rs.68,913/- with interest at 9% per annum.
Challenging the same, the present appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company.
MGP, J Macma_650_2017 6.
Heard both sides and perused the record.

1 7.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd, ... vs Shaik Khaleel, Adilabad Dist 1 Other
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the impugned judgment discloses that the Tribunal has framed issue No.1 as to whether the accident took place on 27.02.2012 due to rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing No. AP 01 H 0564 by its driver, and after considering the evidence of P.W.1 coupled with the documentary evidence i.e., Ex.A1, First Information Report, the tribunal has categorically observed that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle i.e., Car bearing No. AP 01 H 0564 by its driver and has answered the issue in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.
Therefore, I see no reason to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Crime vehicle by its driver.
8. The main contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant is that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

Except the self-serving statement that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving license,
no evidence in that regard was let in before the Tribunal and hence, the Tribunal has MGP, J Macma_650_2017 rightly rejected the said contention.
Therefore, I see no reason to interfere with the said findings of the Tribunal.

9. A perusal of the deposition of PW.2, Doctor at Akil Orthopedic Hospital, reveals that the claimant has sustained one grievous injury i.e., fracture on left leg, due to which, the claimant was unable to walk without crutches.
10. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, according to the claimant, he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month as agriculture coolie.
However, in that regard no oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the claimant to prove his income.

Considering the prevailing minimum rate of wages at the relevant point of time, the Tribunal rightly fixed the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month and rightly awarded Rs.18,000/- towards loss of earnings during the treatment period of six months.

The other amounts awarded by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.30,000/-
towards injury, shock, pain and sufferings; Rs.15,913 towards hospital and medical expenses and Rs.5,000/- towards attendant, transport expenses, are reasonable and needs no interference by this Court.
MGP, J Macma_650_2017 11.
Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A. is dismissed confirming the order and decree passed by the Tribunal.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
_ _ _ JUSTICE M.G. PRIYADARSINI 21.04.2023 gms MGP, J Macma_650_2017 THE HON'BLE SMT.
